name: Beige Grey
lede: Beige Grey is a mid-dark warm neutral, standardized as RAL 7006 in the 1927 color register and filed by ISCC-NBS as a grayish yellowish brown.

sections.title: A register color
sections.body: The library traces the swatch to RAL 7006, first listed in 1927, and to ISCC-NBS block 93 of 1955, whose name for the area is grayish yellowish brown [1]. It is darker than the word suggests, at a lightness of 47 on a 100 scale [1]. Close neighbors are [[quartz-grey]], [[deep-olive]] and [[mouse-grey]] [2].

sections.title: The palette of quiet rooms
sections.body: Pastoureau notes that the barn interiors of Frans Rijckhals (1609 to 1647) work with a palette reduced to browns, beiges, grays and whites, the light doing the work [3]. The same family of dull, warm neutrals fills a great deal of painting, as the numbers below show.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Beige Grey appears in 2,441 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (10.3%), as photographed, more common than 93% of named colors [4]. It peaks in the 1900s at 7.2% of 1,674 paintings, 1.2 times the museums' baseline [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 29% of the 1,346 paintings where it counts [4]. Its most devoted painter is Willem van de Velde the Elder, in 6 of 14 works here, 5.2 times the baseline of his museums but only 1.7 times when read as photographed [4]. The word peaks in printed English in the 1990s [5]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test.
